title: Distributed Tracing
description: Learn distributed tracing to track requests across microservices and debug latency issues.

data.text: Distributed tracing tracks requests as they flow through multiple services, showing the complete journey and identifying bottlenecks. Google, Netflix, and Uber all use distributed tracing to debug latency issues and understand system behavior.

A trace represents the complete journey of a request across services. It consists of spans, each representing a single operation (HTTP call, database query, etc.). Spans have a parent-child relationship, showing the call hierarchy and timing.

data.title: Key Tracing Concepts
items: Trace: Complete request journey across services
Span: Single operation within a trace
Trace ID: Unique identifier linking all spans
Span ID: Unique identifier for each span

data.title: Jaeger
data.text: Jaeger is an open-source distributed tracing platform inspired by Google's Dapper. Netflix, Uber, and Red Hat all use Jaeger for end-to-end request tracing.

data.title: Example: Trace with Spans
data.content: A trace showing a request through multiple services.
data.code:
# Trace: POST /api/orders (trace-id: abc123)

# Span 1: API Gateway (123ms)
#   - Span 2: Order Service (100ms)
#     - Span 3: Inventory Service (40ms)
#     - Span 4: Payment Service (50ms)
#       - Span 5: Database Query (30ms)

# Total: 123ms
# Breakdown:
# - Gateway overhead: 23ms
# - Order Service logic: 10ms
# - Inventory: 40ms
# - Payment: 50ms (including 30ms DB query)

data.caption: Distributed trace spanning multiple services
data.definition:
graph TD
    T[Trace: abc123] --> S1[Span 1: Gateway 123ms]
    S1 --> S2[Span 2: Order 100ms]
    S2 --> S3[Span 3: Inventory 40ms]
    S2 --> S4[Span 4: Payment 50ms]
    S4 --> S5[Span 5: DB Query 30ms]

items.question: How do I propagate trace IDs across services?
items.answer: Pass trace ID and span ID in HTTP headers (traceparent, baggage). W3C Trace Context is the emerging standard for this.

items.question: What is sampling?
items.answer: Tracing every request is expensive. Sampling traces a percentage of requests. Use adaptive sampling to trace more requests during incidents.

items.question: Jaeger vs Zipkin?
items.answer: Jaeger is more modern with better Kubernetes support and OpenTelemetry integration. Zipkin is simpler and mature. Both support OpenTracing API.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Traces show the complete request journey across services
Spans represent individual operations within a trace
Use Jaeger or Zipkin for trace collection and visualization
Propagate trace IDs via HTTP headers
data.takeaway: Distributed tracing is essential for debugging latency in microservices; implement it early.
